items.title: Charles Elgar Interview, 1958-05-27
items.q: Lionel Hampton is on the bill there.

ctx.x: I wondered about their reception, of course the people like myself are more or less a fanatic on the New Orleans style of music, and to me they were so wonderful, just to hear them on the record, what's left. And I wasn't here in those days to hear them, but did they go over unusually well? I mean, did they have the general public or was it just the

certainly the cafe? No, no, no, not at that time. The public hadn't taken to the to the Dixieland idea of music. Of course the music lovers who like that type of thing, they went for it. But not as popular as it is now. You take now, you take these young colleges, these young boys who are in colleges now, my gosh, they go all out for that type of thing. And even having these fellas lecture in these colleges. Duke, Duke has lectured at Yale, at Harvard, all these fine institutions. Look what's happening at…
That's right. But I wondered if the general public, or if it was just the small group, I know it wasn't just the South Side.
